# Intake Brief — Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests (AH-0MUV5CLVQ006V9HR)

**Headline:** Add a dedicated, auto-discovered `GymPowerUpLeveling` demonstration
scene that makes every power-up's (P3–P10) run-scoped level curve observable —
field pickups and hold-full permanent rewards both level the power-up up, and a
live readout shows the resolver-derived stats — plus integration and
game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and assert the shared power-up
level path is byte-for-byte the same in `PlayScene` and the gyms.

## Problem statement

The power-up level model, resolver and store are shipped
(`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`, parent AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6) and wired into the
shared effect path and every scene (AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K, AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB,
AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9), but there is **no dedicated place to see and verify it**
the way weapons have `GymWeaponLeveling`. The existing power-up gyms
(`GymPowerUpsCombat`, `GymPowerUpsUtility`) demonstrate behaviours, not levels;
the parity tests in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boot a
*minimal* `EquivGymScene`, not a real gym, and only exercise a single power-up
(P5). There is therefore a gap in both **legibility** (a producer/designer
cannot watch a power-up level up and see its stats change) and **verification**
(no test proves a shipped gym resolves the level path identically to the game).

## Users

- **Designer / producer (legibility):** "As a designer, I want a gym where I can
  collect a power-up repeatedly and watch its level and resolved stats change,
  so I can sanity-check the curve without reading the catalogue."
- **Engineer (verification):** "As an engineer, I want a test that boots the real
  gym and the game and proves they resolve the same level path for every
  power-up, so a divergent copy cannot slip through."
- **Player (indirect):** "As a player, I want the power-up levels I earn to be
  applied identically everywhere they appear, with no gym-only behaviour."

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Dedicated gym scene.** A new `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts`
  (scene key `GymPowerUpLeveling`, conventional `Gym<Name>.ts` so it is
  auto-discovered by `GymIndex` with no index edit) demonstrates the level
  curve of **every** power-up P3–P10: the operator can collect each power-up
  repeatedly (field drops) and take a hold-full permanent reward, and the scene
  shows the current run-scoped level plus the resolver-derived stats for all
  catalogue variables, updating visibly as the level rises.
- **AC2 — No duplicated model.** The gym reads levels and stats only through the
  shared `PowerUpLevelStore` / `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` (and `EffectsRegistry`);
  it defines no copy of the curve, the catalogue or the level arithmetic, and
  introduces no new shared helper or template-method copy (the duplicate-body
  guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` continues to pass).
- **AC3 — Integration tests.** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts`
  drives the scene deterministically and verifies: field-pickup leveling,
  hold-full permanent leveling, the level readout matches
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel` at representative levels (base / first upgrade /
  mid / cap), every P3–P10 has a growing axis, and the level resets only on run
  restart.
- **AC4 — Game↔gym parity.** Tests boot the real `GymPowerUpLeveling` alongside
  `PlayScene` and assert that, for every power-up P3–P10 across a level sweep
  (0, 1, mid, cap), the run-scoped level, the resolved stats and the observable
  effect-path outputs (e.g. P5 speed multiplier, P8 lives, P3 absorptions, P7
  teleports, P9/P10 stack caps) are identical. The parity assertion lives in the
  shared equivalence test (or a sibling parity test) so the duplicate-body
  guard convention is respected.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** The GDD §4.4.3 status paragraph, the README power-up
  leveling entry and the "Coverage:" lists name the new gym and its tests
  (and any code comments added are accurate).
- **AC6 — Full suite.** The full project test suite passes with the new changes
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope).

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** An enabled gameplay object must run the same
  code in a gym and the game; any behaviour shared by game and gym lives once in
  `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both. No divergent copy.
- **Demonstration only.** This item adds a scene and tests; it must **not**
  change gameplay balance, tuning or the level catalogue. Any balance change
  discovered is a separate linked work item, not scope creep.
- **Auto-discovery convention.** New gym is `src/scenes/gym/Gym<Name>.ts`; the
  scene key equals the class name.
- **Deterministic tests.** Scene tests use the `bootScene` harness and the public
  `tick(dt)` entry point (no real render loop), matching the existing gym tests;
  generous Vitest timeouts are acceptable for Phaser boot.
- **UK English** in all code comments, docs and work-item text.

## Existing state

- **Model shipped:** `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`
  (all P3–P10), pure `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `summarisePowerUpLevelChange`,
  run-scoped `PowerUpLevelStore` on `Player` (`getPowerUpLevel`,
  `getPowerUpLevels`, `resetPowerUpLevels`), shared curve in
  `src/utils/curve.ts`.
- **Effect path wired:** `EffectsRegistry.applyCollect` consumes the player's
  store; P3 `shieldAbsorptions` and P4 `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` axes wired;
  hold-full `ChoiceContext.powerUpLevels` + `power-up-level` offers applied via
  shared `applyMineralChoiceReward`.
- **Precedent:** `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) is the
  weapon-leveling demonstration gym (parent AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J); `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers gyms; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the DOM-panel readout pattern.
- **Existing power-up gyms:** `GymPowerUpsCombat` (P3/P4/P6/P7, threats) and
  `GymPowerUpsUtility` (P5/P8/P9/P10, threat-free) demonstrate behaviour, not
  levels; neither shows a level/stat readout.
- **Existing partial parity:** `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` boots a minimal
  `EquivGymScene` and checks P5 only; `PlayScene.powerUpLevels.test.ts` covers
  the choice path in the game.
- **HUD** (`src/ui/HUD.ts`) renders weapon levels but has no power-up level
  readout.

## Desired change

Add `GymPowerUpLeveling` (auto-discovered) as the canonical place to observe
every power-up's level curve, showing level and resolver-derived stats; add
integration tests for field-pickup and hold-full leveling, the readout and
run-restart reset; and add game↔gym parity tests that boot the real gym and
assert the shared level path matches `PlayScene` for every power-up. Update the
GDD/README references accordingly. No gameplay behaviour changes.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.ts` — **new** demonstration gym scene:
  round-robin/level-up drop source for P3–P10, hold-full permanent path, and a
  level + resolved-stats readout (reusing the shared store/resolver).
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpLeveling.test.ts` — **new** integration tests
  (field pickup, permanent reward, readout vs resolver, reset-on-restart,
  every-power-up-has-an-axis).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend (or add a sibling
  real-gym parity test) to boot `GymPowerUpLeveling` and assert
  `PlayScene`↔gym identity across every power-up and a level sweep; keeps the
  duplicate-body guard authoritative.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **read-only** shared source of truth
  (`POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`, `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStore`); do not
  duplicate.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — shared effect path consumed by the gym (read-only).
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — only if a power-up level readout is added to the shared HUD;
  otherwise the readout stays gym-local (e.g. a `.gym-panel`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4.3 — update the status/coverage sentence to
  name the shipped gym + tests.
- `README.md` — update the power-up leveling entry and its Coverage list.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk (primary):** a demo gym invites "while we're here" gameplay
  or tuning changes. Mitigation: this item is demonstration + tests only; record
  any balance/behaviour opportunity as a separate `discovered-from` item.
- **Threats vs legibility (assumption):** P3/P4/P6/P7 are only fully observable
  under threat; the demonstration gym may include an optional threat toggle
  **or** focus on the resolver/level readout and leave full combat behaviour to
  `GymPowerUpsCombat`. Chosen default: threat-free readout gallery, with an
  optional threat toggle only if needed for the parity tests.
- **HUD coupling (assumption):** the shared HUD has no power-up level readout;
  keep the new readout gym-local to avoid changing shared HUD behaviour.
- **Parity-test flakiness (risk):** booting two Phaser games per case under
  parallel load is slow; reuse the existing generous timeout pattern and a
  single level sweep per power-up rather than many boots.
- **Reset-on-run-restart (ambiguity):** the gym must offer a deterministic way
  to exercise `resetPowerUpLevels` for the reset test; expose a public
  restart/reset hook (test-only seam) rather than relying on a real GameOver.
- **Determinism (constraint):** all tests drive `tick(dt)`, no wall-clock.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6** — Design level curves for all power-ups (parent /
  `discovered-from`). Ships the model this gym demonstrates.
- **AH-0MUV5CLW6005VF7K** — Wire power-up level curves into `EffectsRegistry`
  and the shared effect path (predecessor; makes field pickups level up).
- **AH-0MUVM9RAO004Y3LB** — Wire P3 shield absorption and P4 periodic bomb
  (range/frequency) level axes into the effect path.
- **AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9** — Integrate power-up level-up offers into the
  hold-full choice.
- **AH-0MUWGD0EN008T3TY** — P4 model: `bombRange`/`bombFrequency` replace
  `bombCharges` (supersedes the original P4 axis).
- **AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J** — Weapon-leveling gym demonstration + integration
  tests (the direct structural precedent; mirrors the same shape for weapons).
- **AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA** — Gym↔game behavioural parity: eliminate remaining
  core-code duplication (the parity convention this item must respect).
- **AH-0MUTPEIN0000MDUR** — Test: P10 parity across `PlayScene`, `GymMinerals`
  and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (precedent for real-gym parity tests).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTHG5B83007W4W4** – Single reusable enemy gym scene (GymEnemies) (completed)
- **AH-0MUJSUTXI008NP8K** – Retune the default difficulty curve and seed campaign for playability (completed)
- **AH-0MU44MAAB0007BDD** – Documentation for combat spawning (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, assert, body (+23 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, applies, assert, body, combatscene (+20 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muu2qje2007jnr6, add, applies, body, combatscene (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was conducted: the seed context plus the
shipped model, the wiring predecessors and the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
were sufficient to draft a clear brief (intake SKILL §4 — skip the interview
when seed context suffices; AGENTS.md — do not ask unnecessary questions). Each
apparent design choice is recorded below with the evidence that resolved it and
the documented assumption taken where evidence was partial.

- **Q (resolved from the work item + precedent): Should this be a new dedicated
  gym or an extension of `GymPowerUpsCombat` / `GymPowerUpsUtility`?**
  — Answer: a **new** `GymPowerUpLeveling` scene. Evidence: the work-item title
  and description say "Add a gym scene"; the `GymWeaponLeveling` precedent
  (AH-0MUQOXHWT000XV4J) established a dedicated leveling gym; `GymIndex`
  auto-discovers `Gym<Name>.ts`. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`; `src/utils/gymDiscovery.ts`.
- **Q (resolved from the work item): What is the parity-test scope?**
  — Answer: boot the **real** gym and assert the shared power-up level path is
  identical to `PlayScene`, not another minimal `EquivGymScene`. Evidence: the
  description explicitly requires game↔gym parity "for the shared power-up level
  path" and names the duplicate-body guard. Source: work-item description;
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): Should the gym include combat threats so P3/P4/P6/P7
  behaviour is fully observable?**
  — Answer (assumed, producer may override): threat-free readout gallery as the
  default, with an optional threat toggle only if the parity tests require
  observable combat behaviour. Evidence: `GymWeaponLeveling` is threat-free and
  demonstrates levels via a readout; `GymPowerUpsCombat` already owns the
  threat-based P3/P4/P6/P7 behaviour. Source: `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): What demonstrates "level" — a shared HUD readout or
  a gym-local panel?**
  — Answer (assumed): gym-local readout over `PowerUpLevelStore` /
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`; avoid changing shared HUD behaviour. Evidence: the
  shared HUD has only a weapon-level readout; `GymCurveSequencer` shows the
  established gym-local `.gym-panel` pattern. Source: `src/ui/HUD.ts`,
  `src/scenes/gym/GymCurveSequencer.ts`.
- **Q (assumption recorded): How does the gym exercise level reset?**
  — Answer (assumed): expose a deterministic public restart/reset hook on the
  gym scene so the reset test does not depend on a real GameOver sequence.
  Source: `Player.getPowerUpLevels` / `resetPowerUpLevels`
  (`src/entities/Player.ts`).
- **Observation:** the automated `find-related` report surfaced only generic
  matches (enemy gym, difficulty curve, combat-spawning docs); the higher-signal
  relationships above were found by manual worklog search and file inspection.
data.title: Power-up level gym demonstration and game/gym parity tests

## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halves the enemy `bulletSpeed` of the eight shipped archetypes
across the runtime CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity constants.
During planning, three additional runtime fallbacks were found that also hard-code
`bulletSpeed: 200` for **unknown** archetype keys and were explicitly out of that
item's scope (its Q2 enumeration covered only CSV + defaults + entity constants):

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy would fire at double the speed of
every shipped archetype, so tuning can still drift for that edge case.

## Desired change

Decide and, if accepted, halve these three `bulletSpeed` fallbacks (200 → 100) for
consistency, updating any affected difficulty-sequencer expectations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100` (or a
  documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
- [ ] AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
  change is updated and the full suite passes.
- [ ] AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this item.

## Key Files

- `src/core/configStore.ts`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts`

## Related work

- AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery; strictly out of its scope).

Raised during intake of AH-0MUX802450085VZZ (field pickups must upgrade temporarily). The producer asked us to *consider creating a second power-up type* to represent consumable temporary grants (P6 Phase Shift charges, P7 Teleport stacks) whose unconsumed grants persist until consumed even after the temporary level window expires.

**discovered-from:AH-0MUX802450085VZZ**

## Goal
Evaluate whether consumable temporary grants should be modelled as a distinct power-up type/category rather than as a level that is temporarily raised. This is an *exploratory* task — no code behaviour change is committed until a design decision is made and accepted.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short design note is recorded on this item comparing (a) the level-based temporary model chosen in AH-0MUX802450085VZZ vs (b) a distinct consumable-grant type.
- Recommendation (with rationale) is recorded and the producing work item is linked.
- If a change is recommended, follow-up implementation work items are created; otherwise the item is closed as 'no change required'.

## Notes
- This item is NOT blocking AH-0MUX802450085VZZ, which proceeds with decision (b): unconsumed grants persist until consumed and are not removed on expiry.
data.title: Consider a distinct power-up type for consumable temporary grants (P6/P7)

# Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want a distinct, punchy sound on every boss hit so hits feel responsive and obviously register.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the SFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/audio/effects.ts` exposes the boss cues (`playBossFireSound`, etc.) via the shared ToneForge playback layer.
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` maps every sound-producing cue to a recipe (baked/existing-recipe/runtime-shim) and seeds; `src/audio/cueManifest.ts` is the typed runtime view; `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` enforces completeness.
- Baked WAVs live in `public/audio/sfx/` and are **tracked in git**; recipes live in `audio/toneforge/recipes/`.

## Desired change

1. Add a new recipe `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` producing a short, punchy boss-hit impact (model the YAML shape on `aihell-boss-fire.yaml`).
2. Add a new baked manifest entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`: `{ "cue": "playBossHitSound", "recipe": "aihell-boss-hit", "delivery": "baked", "seeds": [<new seed>] }`.
3. Add `playBossHitSound()` to `src/audio/effects.ts` (delegating to `playCue`).
4. Render and commit the baked WAV `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` via the documented audio build pipeline (`scripts/build-audio.sh` / ToneForge).
5. Add/extend the cue-manifest contract test to require `playBossHitSound`.

## Key Files

- `audio/toneforge/recipes/aihell-boss-hit.yaml` (new).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — new cue entry + seed.
- `public/audio/sfx/aihell-boss-hit.<seed>.wav` (new, committed).
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — `playBossHitSound()`.
- `src/audio/cueManifest.ts`, `src/audio/cueManifest.test.ts` — mapping/contract.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `playBossHitSound` is exported from `src/audio/effects.ts` and appears in `CUE_MANIFEST` with recipe `aihell-boss-hit` and delivery `baked`.
- The recipe YAML exists, is valid, and the baked WAV for its seed is present under `public/audio/sfx/` and tracked.
- The cue-manifest contract test passes and fails if `playBossHitSound` is removed.
- No new runtime dependency is added.
data.title: Add dedicated boss-hit SFX cue

# Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

## Goal / user story

As a player, I want an obvious impact flash at the point where my shot hits the boss — every single hit — so I can see and hear that my fire is connecting.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering the VFX half of parent AC5.

## Existing state

- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` provides `spawnBulletImpact(scene, x, y, options)` (used by `CombatScene` for non-lethal multi-hit enemy feedback on the Harvester) with `radius`/`duration`/`registry` options.
- `src/entities/Boss.ts` `takeDamage()` is the single shared point both `PlayScene._damageBoss()` and `GymBoss.damageBoss()` funnel through; it currently only plays the phase-transition cue on a depleting hit and gives no per-hit feedback.
- `PlayScene.onPlayerBulletHitsBoss` / `onAoeHitsBoss` know the hit point (`pb.x`/`pb.y`); `GymBoss.damageBoss()` damages at the boss centre.

## Desired change

1. Extend `spawnBulletImpact` with an optional `color` option (default unchanged) so boss hits can use a hot impact colour.
2. Change `Boss.takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)` to play `playBossHitSound()` and spawn `spawnBulletImpact` at `(hitX ?? this.x, hitY ?? this.y)` on **every** landed hit. Retain the existing phase-transition cue on a depleting hit.
3. Track per-hit VFX in a small registry (`_hitEffects`) for test observability, removed on completion and torn down in `destroy()`.
4. Thread the hit point through `PlayScene._damageBoss(hitX?, hitY?)` from `onPlayerBulletHitsBoss`/`onAoeHitsBoss`; the gym calls `takeDamage()` at the boss centre.
5. Keep the feedback in the shared `Boss.takeDamage()` path so the game and gym cannot diverge.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Boss.ts` — `takeDamage(hitX?, hitY?)`, hit VFX/SFX, registry, teardown.
- `src/vfx/bulletImpact.ts` — optional `color` option.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — thread hit point through `_damageBoss`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — gym uses the shared path.
- `src/entities/Boss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/vfx/bulletImpact.test.ts` — feedback tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every boss hit registers exactly one impact VFX at the supplied hit point (or the boss centre when none) and plays `playBossHitSound`.
- A depleting hit still plays the existing phase-transition cue in addition to the per-hit cue/VFX.
- Both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` receive the same feedback because it lives in shared `Boss.takeDamage()`.
- The VFX registry is emptied on completion and on `destroy()` (no leak / no orphan Graphics).
- Tests assert an impact effect is registered per hit and at the expected coordinates.

**Parent AC traceability (mirrors parent AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X):**
- (parent AC5) **Hits on the boss are obvious with both SFX and VFX.** Every hit on the boss plays a dedicated boss-hit SFX cue and spawns an obvious impact VFX (flash/burst) at the hit point; phase transitions retain their existing distinct cue and visual. Game and gym use the same shared feedback path. Verified by the cue-manifest contract test (new cue registered) and VFX tests (an impact effect is registered per hit).
data.title: Add per-hit boss impact VFX on shared feedback path

# Verify gym-game parity and full test suite

## Goal / user story

As a developer, I want proof that the new boss behaviour is identical in the game and the boss gym, and that the whole suite is green, before the epic is reviewed.

This is part of parent Enhance Central AI boss encounter (AH-0MUY3X4NS007JR8X), covering parent AC6 and AC8.

# Report script counts soft-deleted children

**discovered-from:AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2**

## Problem

The canonical end-of-session report (`skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) shows an incorrect **Children** count when a parent has soft-deleted children.

- `wl delete <id>` is a **soft delete** — it sets `status=deleted` and `deletedBy`, and the item remains visible via `wl show <parent> --children`.
- `wl list --parent <id>` correctly **excludes** deleted items.
- `render_report.py` (`render_from_wl`) counts `len(data["children"])` from `wl show --children`, so it **includes** the tombstones.

Observed on AH-0MUZMTTYH008KVS2: 7 active children + 6 soft-deleted coverage-gap children reported as `Children: 13`; `wl list --parent` correctly reports 7.

## Expected behaviour

The report's child count matches the active child set — i.e. it excludes items with `status=deleted` (or `deletedBy` set). Ideally the shared `wl show --children` behaviour and the report agree with `wl list --parent`.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a parent with children.
2. `wl delete <one-child> --json` (soft delete).
3. Run `python3 skill/report/scripts/render_report.py <parent-id> --skill-name plan ...`.
4. Observe the **Children** count includes the deleted child.

## Suggested fix

Filter deleted children in `render_from_wl` before counting (e.g. `[c for c in children if c.get("status") != "deleted" and not c.get("deletedBy")]`), or make `wl show --children` exclude deleted items consistently with `wl list --parent`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The report's **Children** count excludes soft-deleted items.
- A test covers a parent with a mix of active and soft-deleted children.
- Behaviour is consistent with `wl list --parent`.

# Pac-Man ghost personality pursuers

Part of epic **Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old** (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52).
Design brief: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` (selected archetype: **Pac-Man**).
Implements one selected classic-arcade archetype as a full vertical slice
(config, entity, tests, code comments, gym parity).

## User story

As a player, I want a set of pursuers each with its own personality - one that chases directly, one that ambushes ahead of me, one that flanks and one that wanders - alternating between scatter and chase, so that dodging them is about reading distinct behaviours rather than one homing blob.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Pac-Man (Namco, 1980)
- **Original behaviour:** Four ghosts leave a central pen and pursue Pac-Man with distinct targeting rules (direct chase, ambush ahead, flank via a pivot, random wander), alternating scatter and chase phases on a timer.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** Four fast, low-HP pursuers spawn from arena edges or a pen and steer with distinct personalities: `chase` (direct pursuit), `ambush` (target ahead of the player's velocity), `flank` (target a pivot point offset from the player) and `wander` (bounded random walk). A shared scatter/chase timer alternates their target modes. They pass through each other (no enemy-enemy collision), never shoot (enemies-are-the-bullets: body contact is lethal), and are worth points like other enemies.

## Pipeline fit

New entity plus a dynamic spawner, because the personalities are a steering behaviour no formation expresses. Data-driven via CSV rows (one row per personality or a new `personality` column); non-firing archetypes get an explicit `tryFireNone` entry so they never fall back to the aimed shot.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count`, `driftSpeed` (pursuit speed), `formationKind` (`single`), `shotPattern` (`none`), `health` (1). Personalities are a steering variant, not a new scoring axis.

## Gym parity

`GymEnemies` (live player) for steering and contact; the shared core keeps game/gym parity.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Ghost.ts` - New. Pursuer with personalities.
- `src/waves/GhostSpawner.ts` - New. Dynamic wave-accounted spawner.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` / `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` - Updated. Rows / personality field.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` - Updated. Seed fallbacks.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` - Updated. Factory + `tryFireNone` dispatch.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` - Exercised for parity with a live player.

## Implementation plan (follows ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md section 8.6)

1. Tune steering in a gym with a live player; define each personality's target function.
2. Add `src/entities/Ghost.ts` with a personality selector and the standard entity seam.
3. Add a dynamic spawner (`src/waves/GhostSpawner.ts`, modelled on `AsteroidSpawner`) so the four personalities enter as a wave-accounted group.
4. Add CSV rows (one per personality, or one row plus a personality column) and seed fallbacks; register the factory/fire-dispatch entry.
5. Unit-test each personality's target function, the scatter/chase alternation, and wave accounting; parity-test the shared path.
6. Run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-archetype child for Pac-Man: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and an implementation plan following section 8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and references the epic AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52 and `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- The archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- The archetype's notes name the gym scene(s) that exercise it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) for gym-to-game parity, and the implemented behaviour runs the same shared code in the gym and the game (enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- Four distinct steering personalities (`chase`, `ambush`, `flank`, `wander`) each produce a different deterministic target for the same world state, pinned by unit tests.
- A shared scatter/chase timer alternates the pursuers' target modes on a configured cadence; the alternation is a pure function of time and is unit-tested.
- Pursuers never fire at any level, and body contact uses the existing enemy-body death rule; both are verified by tests.
- Every spawned pursuer is registered with the wave accounting so the wave neither clears early nor stalls (same invariant as the Asteroid/Harvester spawners).
- Unit and integration tests exist for the archetype's movement, firing/telegraphing (if any) and wave accounting; every acceptance criterion is covered by an automated test.
- Full project test suite passes with the new archetype and all new tests.

As a player, I want a snake-like chain of segments that weaves down the arena and splits into two independent chains when I shoot a middle segment, so that clearing it is a satisfying chain-management puzzle.

- **Source:** Centipede (Atari, 1981)
- **Original behaviour:** A centipede of linked segments snakes across and down the playfield, reversing at edges; shooting a middle segment splits the chain into two independent chains; each lost segment makes the rest faster.

Segments pass through each other and other enemies (no enemy-enemy collision) and never fire. Every spawned segment is wave-accounted so the wave cannot clear early or stall, following the Asteroid split precedent.

New entity plus a dynamic spawner, because a linked chain is not expressible as a formation. A chain-split difficulty axis analogous to `asteroidSplit` may be proposed in the design phase; otherwise reuse the existing factors.

`count` (segments), `driftSpeed`, `formationKind`, `shotPattern` (`none`), `health` (1), plus a proposed chain-split count factor analogous to `asteroidSplit` if adopted by the scoring module.

## User story

As a player, I want a telegraphed incoming strike that marks its impact point before a fast projectile falls and detonates, so I must keep moving and read the warning rather than react to an instantaneous hit.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Missile Command (Atari, 1980)
- **Original behaviour:** Incoming missiles appear at the top of the screen and track down toward cities/ground, detonating on impact; the player intercepts them.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** A target marker/warning appears at a predicted impact point near the player, holds for a configurable tell (at least 500 ms, matching the Phaser telegraph convention), then a fast projectile falls from off-screen and detonates in a radial burst at that point. This is a world hazard, not a wave-gating enemy ship: it does not count toward wave completion (same non-blocking accounting as asteroids), and it respects no enemy-enemy collision.

## Pipeline fit

New hazard entity plus a dynamic spawner (the asteroid precedent), and possibly a new `EnemyShotPattern` (`strike`) for the telegraph+radial burst. Data-driven via CSV columns.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count`, `shotPattern` (new strike/radial), `bulletSpeed`, `bulletLifetime`, `burstCount`, `fireInterval` (strike cadence), `health` (1).

## Gym parity

- `src/utils/enemyShotPatterns.ts` - Updated. Strike/telegraph pattern registration (if adopted).

# Frogger lane traffic hazard

Part of epic **Research classic enemies from the arcade games of old** (AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52).
Design brief: `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md` (selected archetype: **Frogger**).
Implements one selected classic-arcade archetype as a full vertical slice
(config, entity, tests, code comments, gym parity).

## User story

As a player, I want lanes of fast traffic crossing the arena that I must weave through or shoot, so the arena has a moving spatial hazard distinct from homing enemies.

## Source and adaptation

- **Source:** Frogger (Konami/Sega, 1981)
- **Original behaviour:** Lanes of cars/logs cross the screen at constant speed; a collision with a car is fatal and the player must time crossings.
- **AI_Hell adaptation:** One to three traffic lanes cross the arena at constant speed and wrap at the edges; the hazards never fire and do not home. They are destructible (one player bullet each) to fit the enemies-are-the-bullets design and the asteroid/obstacle model, and they are non-blocking for wave completion (the asteroid accounting). They pass through each other and other enemies (no enemy-enemy collision).

## Pipeline fit

New hazard entity plus a dynamic spawner (asteroid precedent), or a reuse of the existing obstacle entity if its seam covers wrapping lanes. Data-driven via CSV columns; non-blocking wave accounting.

## Difficulty scoring inputs

`count` (per lane), `driftSpeed` (lane speed), `formationKind` (`single`/`rect`), `shotPattern` (`none`), `health` (1).

## Gym parity

`GymEnemies` (live player) for lane hazards; `GymLevel` may exercise them in a wave context. Shared core keeps parity.

## Key Files

- `src/entities/Traffic.ts` - New (or reuse/extend `src/entities/Obstacle.ts`). Lane hazard.
- `src/waves/TrafficSpawner.ts` - New. Non-blocking dynamic spawner.
- `src/core/configTypes.ts` / `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` - Updated. Lane fields and row.
- `src/core/configDefaults.ts` - Updated. Seed fallback.
- `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` / `src/entities/enemyFire.ts` - Updated. Factory + `tryFireNone`.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymEnemies.ts` - Exercised for parity (or `GymLevel`).

## Implementation plan (follows ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md section 8.6)

1. Tune lane count, lane position, speed, spacing and wrap in a gym with a live player.
2. Add `src/entities/Traffic.ts` (or reuse/extend the existing obstacle entity) with the standard seam.
3. Add `src/waves/TrafficSpawner.ts` (modelled on `AsteroidSpawner`) with non-blocking wave accounting.
4. Add config/CSV fields (lane, speed, spacing) and seed fallbacks; register factory/fire-dispatch (`tryFireNone`).
5. Unit-test constant-speed motion, edge wrap, spacing, destructibility and non-blocking accounting; parity-test the shared path.
6. Run the full suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- This work item is the per-selected-archetype child for Frogger: it contains a user story, measurable/testable acceptance criteria including unit tests, predicted key files, and an implementation plan following section 8.6 "Adding a new enemy" in `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, and references the epic AH-0MUYAQ6YH0010G52 and `docs/CLASSIC_ENEMY_RESEARCH.md`.
- The archetype's design notes specify how it fits the data-driven pipeline, i.e. whether it is expressible as an `EnemyConfig`/CSV row or needs a new `src/entities/<Name>.ts` plus factory/fire-dispatch seam, and give its enemy difficulty scoring inputs (movement / fire / health factors).
- The archetype's notes name the gym scene(s) that exercise it (existing `GymEnemies` or a new gym) for gym-to-game parity, and the implemented behaviour runs the same shared code in the gym and the game (enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- One or more traffic lanes cross the arena at constant speed and wrap at the edges; the motion and wrap are unit-tested.
- Traffic hazards never fire and are destructible by a single player bullet (1 HP); both are verified by tests.
- Traffic is a non-blocking hazard: it is not registered with wave completion (asteroid accounting), verified by a test.
- Traffic hazards pass through each other and other enemies (no enemy-enemy collision), verified by a test.
- Unit and integration tests exist for the archetype's movement, firing/telegraphing (if any) and wave accounting; every acceptance criterion is covered by an automated test.
- Full project test suite passes with the new archetype and all new tests.

data.description:
discovered-from:AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A

## Problem

Several deterministic bot micro-simulations are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1-5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:
- src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts - synthetic human seed moved 7 -> 14.
- src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts - RUN_SEED moved 0x0b07 -> 0x0b16.

On the base behaviour, src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts already regressed on 13/24 seeds, and the competent-vs-legacy AC6 test only wins in base because the legacy bot chaotically collides with bullets; without bullets the legacy bot scored higher (22 vs 20) on base.

## Goal

Make these tests robust rather than seed-picked:
- Aggregate competence/style comparisons over a set of seeds (e.g. assert the styled/competent bot is not systematically worse), or
- Compare on scenarios whose score is not dominated by discrete collisions.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The style-match AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed (e.g. asserts over multiple seeds).
- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 test asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions.
- AC3: Recalibrating either test is not required by an unrelated small bot-feel tweak.
- AC4: Full test suite, typecheck and build pass.
data.title: Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks
